text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The West is bewildered by the rapid growth of the Turkish economy despite ongoing political instability.
- Turks living in Europe face the threat of racism after three recent arson attacks against Turkish families there.
- President Suleyman Demirel attempts to block the dismissal of Turkey's police chief in a letter sent to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
- Erbakan says he opposes eight-year compulsory education, which he says would cost $40 billion. He supports a two stage, eight-year plan.
- The head of a contra-guerilla squad says the state is involved in the murder of secularist journalist Ugur Mumcu in a car-bomb attack.
- Turkish troops kill 56 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militants in clashes in the mainly Kurdish populated southeast in three days.
- Istanbul is the 15th most expensive city in the world according to a research carried out by International Runzheimer.
- The United States will host a joint military exercises in June involving Turkey and Greece.
